acceptance_criteria: Mailbox/get with properties:[name] returns objects with only id and name fields; id is always present even when not listed in properties; Email/get properties filtering tested for at least 3 property subsets
close_reason: filter_properties moved to helpers.rs, applied in mailbox/thread/identity get handlers; 5 new property-filter tests
description: All /get handlers (Mailbox/get, Email/get, Thread/get, Identity/get, etc.) currently serialize and return the full object regardless of the properties argument. RFC 8620 §5.1 requires that only the requested properties are returned. The RFC expert ruling in rfc-clarifications.md Q8 confirms: id is always included; no unrequested properties should be returned. This affects all /get handlers in jmap-mail-server.
design:
The fix has two parts:

1. Parse the properties argument in each /get handler. If Some([...]), filter the serialized JSON object to only include those keys plus id (id is always included even if not listed — Q8 ruling). If None, return all fields.

2. The filtering can be done as a shared helper: fn filter_properties(obj: Value, props: Option<&[String]>) -> Value. If props is None, return obj unchanged. Otherwise, keep only keys that are in props, always keeping id.

Affected handlers: handle_mailbox_get, handle_email_get, handle_thread_get, handle_identity_get, handle_submission_get, handle_vacation_get, handle_search_snippet_get.

Note: Email/get has additional complexity (bodyProperties, fetchTextBodyValues, fetchHtmlBodyValues, fetchAllBodyValues, maxBodyValueBytes) which is already handled separately. The fix here is only for the top-level properties filtering.

Ref: rfc-clarifications.md Q8; RFC 8620 §5.1; jmap-test-suite get-metadata-properties test.
title: jmap-mail-server: /get handlers ignore properties arg, return all fields
